A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

edits.description: publish: small changes Claude makes to the file at `file_path` in this same call, instead of editing the file with Edit and publishing after. Use it on a page (add `url` to update an artifact from another conversation) or on one data file of an artifact made from a type (its `url`, with that file as `file_path`). Not allowed with `type_url`, `files` or `root`. Each old_str is text copied exactly from the file as it now stands and must occur in it exactly once; new_str takes its place (empty deletes it). The edits apply in order, all or none: the file is published with them and then saved with them on disk, so it stays the source for later changes; on a miss nothing is changed or published, and the result says which edit failed and why.

old_str.description: Text copied exactly from the file; must occur once.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"I committed `31a9c2d` on `v1` (`docs(v1): record wave 1 of the meeting follow-ups`). It changes only `docs/v1/{DECISIONS,CONTRACTS,STATUS,PLAN}.md` and the « Langues » section of `CLAUDE.md`, all in French. I took the test results you gave me as given and did not rerun anything.

**DECISIONS.md**
- New entries dated 2026-10-15: D-369, D-370, D-374 to D-377 and D-382 to D-388 in a new technical subsection, and D-371 in a new subsection under the game rules. D-372, D-373 and D-378 to D-381 are named as reserved in the subsection intro, but not written.
- D-387 records what was built, not what the plan said: the CJK fallback fonts are set at run time for the active language only (`LhtFonts`), not baked into the theme. Baking them in raised every line height and broke `test_results_layout` in French.
- D-371 also covers `layout.Slots`, since it is already used by the automatic layout, the bots and the balance model. I did not open D-372 for it.
- Old entries are unchanged apart from appended "→ révisé/précisé par" pointers. Beyond the list you gave for D-369, I also added pointers on D-071 and D-244 (construction state and refusal), D-290 (scaffold banners), D-252, D-004 and D-198.
- The A1 and A3 annex headers got a note pointing to D-371 and D-369; the table values are untouched.

**CONTRACTS.md**
- Construction removed everywhere: conventions line, catalog example and building rules, events (`building_upgraded {building_id, level}` replaces `construction_*`), revisions text, §4.7 village (no `construction` field, no `constructing` state, no 409), console (no `finish`), `buildings` table and migration 0064, background loop.
- Grid capacity can be `null` (unlimited) in the catalog, sync, layout and `grid_expanded`; `capacity_exceeded` applies only to a capped grid.
- §7 client: `settings.json` gets the optional `language` field; new « Langues » bullet for the `godot/i18n` conventions; local placement checks (capacity only when set, 256-tower bound); `CombatHud` and `SegmentedHpBar` APIs with compact mode; immediate upgrades in the village module; `WorldBanner` with neutral dividers; new `model_for_state(id, state)` signature.
- The compact mode is not used in game yet: the contract says the combat module still shows only the full banner until the free-combat work in wave 2.

**STATUS.md**: a new section « Retours de réunion du 2026-10-15 — vague 5.1 » with one row per subject and the verification table:

| Subject | State | Main gap |
|---|---|---|
| Langues | 🟡 foundation only | text extraction and translated screen captures come later |
| Construction | ✅ | real-server E2E tests updated but not rerun; captures to retake |
| Tours | 🟡 server done | client display and rebalance are wave 2 |
| PV du titan | ✅ | — |
| Combat libre | ❌ | wave 2 |

- **Verification:** Go is 32 of 33 packages, with `TestWorldTitansDieInThreeToSixVisits` red as expected until the rebalance. Godot is 777 passed, 0 failed, lint has 0 WARNING, and art checks pass (7674 checks). The migration 0064 test passes, and the combat capture list now has 15 views.
- **Known limits from the reviews:** among them, a console-saved defense of more than 256 towers now reaches the engine and fails there instead of getting a clean refusal.

**PLAN.md**
- New « Vague 5 — Retours de réunion du 2026-10-15 » section in §3, covering the four sub-waves 5.1 to 5.4, with branches, path ownership and merge order (from the critique §1), plus the reserved decision blocks.
- The capture list is updated: combat has 15 views, and the art gallery no longer has buildings under construction.
- The village E2E line is updated: it no longer advances the server clock, and its check count needs measuring again.
- The server test line notes the expected red test until the rebalance.
- `combat_hud` is removed from the « Passe interface » to-do list, now that it is a scene.

content.content:
Branch g (towers B) is done. All balance criteria pass again, the full Go suite passes (33/33), and the worktree is clean. The branch was reset to v1 at 242a384 before any work.

What I changed:

1. **Code: wave 1 had already switched to `layout.Slots`; I cleaned up after it.**
   - `balance/reference.go` and `balance/player.go`: the leftover `capacity` variables are renamed `slots`, and the comments now say fusion only happens beyond Slots+2.
   - `msq/balance_test.go`: the report column is labelled "slots".

2. **Perf and load generator.**
   - `perf/scenarios_test.go`: new `filledDefense`. The three `*_maxgrid` inputs now hold exactly 75 towers: the reference player who finished the quest owns 53, so basic-chest towers bought after the quest fill the rest. `TestScenariosAreFights` now checks that every scenario on the largest grid fills exactly Slots (the assertion planned in plan B).
   - `cmd/lht-loadgen`: new `giveTowers` gives towers through the console in batches of 50, which is the console's per-call limit (`maxDevTowers`). `bigfight` gives one tower per anchor (75 on a maze or in walls). `burst` gives one tower per slot of the tier's grid (52 at tier 10) instead of 20. New test: `TestGiveTowersBatchesTheConsoleCalls`.
   - `tools/perf/README.md`: "20 tours" becomes "75 tours", and the longest-path search now takes about 20 s instead of 5 min.

3. **Data retune (titans.json and world.json only; msq.json and hunts.json are unchanged).**
   - **Quest titans:** HP chosen so the reference player kills each tier about as often as before (D-167), using a temporary HP-scan test that was not committed.
   - **Hunts:** same method, matching the kill rates of D-172 and D-273.
   - **World titans:** HP per player ×3, which brings back the D-224 visit counts.
   - **World gold:** `hp_per_gold` ×3, so a visit pays the same gold as before.
   - **Tiers 5 and 6:** set below the quick-test target, because in the time simulation the slow profile stalled on tier 6. The longest stall was 3:36 at 2650 HP and 3:09 at 2500 HP, both over the 3:00 limit; at 2400 HP it is 1:35.

**Changed data fields (old → new):**

|---|---|---|
| titans.json | msq_02 max_hp | 300 → 760 |
| titans.json | msq_03 max_hp | 440 → 1050 |

| world.json | hp_per_gold | 50 → 150 |

Unchanged: msq_01 (150) and hunt_01 (80), because the starting kit must always kill them.

**C3 review (role of fusion beyond Slots+2).**
- C3 still passes ("fusion 1≤1"), but it only checks that the workshop is affordable before tier 2.
- The fixed reference player now never fuses. They own 6 to 48 towers against 14 to 52 slots, and fusion only starts at Slots+2. So the D-179 calibration no longer relies on fusion, and the {fusion, 2} expectation is empty in practice.
- In the time simulation, the workshop only uses towers the grid cannot hold, and there are now few of those. Per reference player (median): fusions 6–11 (v1: 21–39), transfers 2–3 (v1: 5–17), neighbour catalysts used 0 (v1: 12–95). The slow profile makes 5–16 fusions (v1: 22–29).

All reports are under `C:\Users\akitl\AppData\Local\Temp\lht-v1-w2-towers-balance\reports` and `...\perf`. 
TESTS Machine: i5-12500 (6 performance cores, no efficiency cores), shared with other agents. It is not the reference machine of STATUS §45, so I measured v1 and the branch side by side on this machine.

- `TestEveryTierIsBeatenByTheReferencePlayer`, `TestHuntsAreBeatenByTheReferencePlayer`, `TestHuntCooldownsLeaveTheReferenceGold`.

content.content:
The player can now move freely during a fight, following plan_cam.md with critique §2 "cam" corrections 1-5 and the user's decisions. The branch is reset onto v1 (242a384), has three commits, and the worktree is clean.

**Server**
- `workshop.Transfer` now refuses a placed receiver with 409 `layout_locked` (`locked_until`, `tower_id`) while `layout.LockedUntil` reports an active lock. The check comes after the donor check, under the player lock that `begin` takes, so it is serialized with the creation of an encounter. There is no import cycle.
- The doc comment that said "the receiver may be placed" is updated.
- `app/strict_test.go` has no per-route error table, so nothing to declare there.
- Two new Go tests:
  - `TestTransferOntoAPlacedTowerWaitsForTheEndOfTheLayoutLock`: a placed receiver is refused while locked (no gold spent, nothing consumed), a receiver outside the defense is accepted during the lock, and the placed one is accepted once the lock is over.
  - `TestTransferWaitsForAnEncounterBeingCreated`: a transfer blocks on the player lock held by an uncommitted encounter creation, then gets `layout_locked`.

**Client: what is locked during a fight**
- The rename is done everywhere: `set_interaction_locked`/`is_interaction_locked` become `set_map_locked`/`is_map_locked` (8 code files, 15 test files, godot/README).
- `Valley.set_map_locked` locks only the map:
  - the parchment closes, still with the warning when unsaved changes are dropped;
  - P is refused and shows the toast "Disposition verrouillée pendant le combat.";
  - the HUD's Parchemin button is disabled with that text as its tooltip (the icons-only bar mode is handled too);
  - `ValleySelection.set_towers_pickable(false)` takes towers out of picking and selection and drops a selected tower and its card.
- Views (V, 1, 2 and the HUD buttons), the menu and its settings, buildings, the QG button and every village panel stay usable. The now-unused `ValleySelection.set_enabled` is removed.
- Village module: panels no longer close when a fight starts and the QG button is always shown.
  - The Temple reloads its codex when the active encounter changes, so it still never shows the codex during a fight (D-159).
  - The Hut uses `LaunchLock.reason(fight_shown, world_visit)`, recomputed on every tick, with "Un combat est en cours : lancez le suivant après « Continuer »." taking priority over the world-visit reason. After launching a hunt it stays open and reloads its offers.
  - The Workshop gets `map_locked` and re-renders when the lock changes. `TransferSelection.receiver_refusal` (new `LAYOUT_LOCKED`) is used by `preview` and by the receiver list: placed towers are disabled with a note, and the preview refuses.

**Client: camera and banner**
- `CombatValleyPort` gains `current_view` and the `view_changed` signal; the test stand-in valley implements them.
- The combat module adds `_launched_here`: only a fight launched by this client moves the camera to Defense. An automatic engagement, a resume or a fight that follows another does not.
- `_apply_view` calls `_hud.set_compact(view != defense)` and hides the damage numbers outside Defense. `set_watch_available(true)` is set and `watch_requested` goes to `focus_view(defense)`.
- Results call `move_to_front()` so they show in front of the village panels, and « Continuer » never moves the camera.
- `test_fight_screen_has_no_playback_control` is scoped to the full banner (no button), plus a check that the compact banner has only "Voir le combat".
- The compact announcement now wraps to two lines instead of being cut off.

**Presentation hold (§17)**
- New `GameState` methods:
  - `note_own_spending(gold, qg)`: only during a hold; works on a copy of the player, never below 0; emits `player_changed`, `resources_changed` and the new `held_spending_applied`.
  - `apply_village(data, own)`: shows the village at once with the displayed QG points.
  - `apply_own_inventory(added, removed, item_deltas)`: uses the new `InventoryModel.apply_local_change`, which keeps the revision.
  - `mask_held_balance(error)`: replaces `available` in `insufficient_gold`, `insufficient_qg_points` and `missing_catalyst` with the displayed value.
- Callers:
  - `VillageService.upgrade` takes the cost from the displayed `next_level`.
  - `MerchantService` and `WorkshopService` now take `(gateway, state)`; during a hold their result's `gold` is the displayed balance.
  - `EncounterService.start_hunt(hunt_id, bait_gold)` takes the bait cost unless the answer is a replay; the combat module passes the catalog's bait cost.
- The HUD refreshes on `held_spending_applied` even while frozen. The server state is applied at « Continuer ».

**Capture (read)**
- New view `fight_merchant` in `village_capture_stage`, with two new shots added to `village.json`: a main quest fight reported by the server, followed from the Village view with the Merchant open.
- Windowed captures at 1920×1080 and 1280×720 (`errors=0`), which I read. They show the compact banner (Golem des cendres, segmented bar with markers, 61 %, the two-line announcement, "Voir le combat") at the top centre, the Merchant panel on the right, Parchemin greyed out, QG visible and the Village view active.
- Files: `C:/Users/akitl/AppData/Local/Temp/lht-v1-w2-combat-free-view/shots/village_fight_merchant_{1920x1080,1280x720}.png`. 
TESTS Godot (`C:/travaille/godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe`, headless):

As a result, a hunt whose creation answer was lost never had its bait taken from the displayed gold, whether the fight came back through the retry with the same key or through GET /v1/encounters/current. The displayed gold then stayed above the server's during the hold, and mask_held_balance produced refusals like 'Or insuffisant : 250 requis, 300 disponible.' Fix: the bait is now taken once per hunt encounter id (new _baits_noted), whatever the replayed flag says. A transient failure of start_hunt records the creation in doubt (_doubtful_hunt and _doubtful_bait). fetch_current settles that doubt: if the current encounter is that hunt, its bait is taken; the doubt is cleared in every case. A successful creation, or a refusal other than encounter_in_progress, also clears the doubt; encounter_in_progress keeps it because the flow then resumes. A stale answer naming a hunt already paid is not paid again. Tests added in godot/tests/core/state/test_held_operations.gd: replayed answer from the gateway's own retry, lost answer then retry, lost answer then resume (taken once even if resumed twice), lost request that created nothing (nothing taken), stale replay of a paid hunt (not paid twice). The player can now move freely during a fight, following plan_cam.md with critique §2 "cam" corrections 1-5 and the user's decisions. The branch is reset onto v1 (242a384), has three commits, and the worktree is clean.

**Server**
- `workshop.Transfer` now refuses a placed receiver with 409 `layout_locked` (`locked_until`, `tower_id`) while `layout.LockedUntil` reports an active lock. The check comes after the donor check, under the player lock that `begin` takes, so it is serialized with the creation of an encounter. There is no import cycle.
- The doc comment that said "the receiver may be placed" is updated.
- `app/strict_test.go` has no per-route error table, so nothing to declare there.
- Two new Go tests:
  - `TestTransferOntoAPlacedTowerWaitsForTheEndOfTheLayoutLock`: a placed receiver is refused while locked (no gold spent, nothing consumed), a receiver outside the defense is accepted during the lock, and the placed one is accepted once the lock is over.
  - `TestTransferWaitsForAnEncounterBeingCreated`: a transfer blocks on the player lock held by an uncommitted encounter creation, then gets `layout_locked`.

**Client: what is locked during a fight**
- The rename is done everywhere: `set_interaction_locked`/`is_interaction_locked` become `set_map_locked`/`is_map_locked` (8 code files, 15 test files, godot/README).
- `Valley.set_map_locked` locks only the map:
  - the parchment closes, still with the warning when unsaved changes are dropped;
  - P is refused and shows the toast "Disposition verrouillée pendant le combat.";
  - the HUD's Parchemin button is disabled with that text as its tooltip (the icons-only bar mode is handled too);
  - `ValleySelection.set_towers_pickable(false)` takes towers out of picking and selection and drops a selected tower and its card.
- Views (V, 1, 2 and the HUD buttons), the menu and its settings, buildings, the QG button and every village panel stay usable. The now-unused `ValleySelection.set_enabled` is removed.
- Village module: panels no longer close when a fight starts and the QG button is always shown.
  - The Temple reloads its codex when the active encounter changes, so it still never shows the codex during a fight (D-159).
  - The Hut uses `LaunchLock.reason(fight_shown, world_visit)`, recomputed on every tick, with "Un combat est en cours : lancez le suivant après « Continuer »." taking priority over the world-visit reason. After launching a hunt it stays open and reloads its offers.
  - The Workshop gets `map_locked` and re-renders when the lock changes. `TransferSelection.receiver_refusal` (new `LAYOUT_LOCKED`) is used by `preview` and by the receiver list: placed towers are disabled with a note, and the preview refuses.

**Client: camera and banner**
- `CombatValleyPort` gains `current_view` and the `view_changed` signal; the test stand-in valley implements them.
- The combat module adds `_launched_here`: only a fight launched by this client moves the camera to Defense. An automatic engagement, a resume or a fight that follows another does not.

- New `GameState` methods:
  - `note_own_spending(gold, qg)`: only during a hold; works on a copy of the player, never below 0; emits `player_changed`, `resources_changed` and the new `held_spending_applied`.

  - `mask_held_balance(error)`: replaces `available` in `insufficient_gold`, `insufficient_qg_points` and `missing_catalyst` with the displayed value.

lines: Une rencontre acquittée dans la session n'est plus jamais signalée active (une synchronisation partie avant l'acquittement arrive parfois après lui), et le verrou de la disposition qu'elle posait (disposition lue pendant le combat) est levé. Les signaux de `GameState` passent des copies : un écouteur qui modifie l'état ne change pas l'argument reçu par les suivants.

-Seul le présentateur (le module combat) réclame (`claim_presentation`) et lève (`release_presentation`) une retenue. Une rencontre que personne ne présente est libérée dès que le serveur ne la signale plus (acquittée ailleurs, expirée). Les modules village et monde ne lèvent jamais une retenue : ils lisent l'état affiché (ou `confirmed_*` pour une décision), et réagissent aux signaux, qui arrivent au bon moment. Un module monde démarre un combat par `start_world_engagement(visit_id)` du module combat.

+Seul le présentateur (le module combat) réclame (`claim_presentation`) et lève (`release_presentation`) une retenue. Une rencontre que personne ne présente est libérée dès que le serveur ne la signale plus (acquittée ailleurs, expirée). Les opérations du joueur pendant une retenue (amélioration, coffre, atelier, appât d'une chasse) s'affichent aussitôt sur l'état affiché (`note_own_spending`, `apply_village(data, own)`, `apply_own_inventory`) et les soldes d'un refus sont masqués (`mask_held_balance`) : l'affichage montre l'état d'avant le combat, moins les dépenses du joueur, plus ses propres résultats, jamais la récompense. Les modules village et monde ne lèvent jamais une retenue : ils lisent l'état affiché (ou `confirmed_*` pour une décision), et réagissent aux signaux, qui arrivent au bon moment. Un module monde démarre un combat par `start_world_engagement(visit_id)` du module combat.

-`scenes/valley/valley.tscn` (cible de « Jouer », `SceneRouter.VALLEY`) : la vallée à la grille du palier MSQ, caméras Défense / Village, tours du layout et chemin en 3D, sélection (fiche de tour en haut à gauche, qui s'arrête au-dessus de l'entrée de la grille et défile au-delà ; un bâtiment émet un signal sans bouger la caméra), HUD, parchemin, menu en jeu (au-dessus de l'alerte du titan mondial, fermé au début d'un combat : un combat ne se met pas en pause ; couches : HUD et panneaux 10, parchemin 20, alerte du titan 25, menu en jeu 30, fondu 40, Overlay 50). L'étiquette de survol suit l'état du bâtiment ou de la tour survolés (village, layout, inventaire) ; elle disparaît au début d'un changement de vue et dès que le pointeur passe sur l'interface. Le HUD garde sa barre d'actions dans les marges quelle que soit l'échelle : version compacte (texte et marges réduits), puis icônes seules (le nom reste dans l'infobulle) ; quête finie : « Quête terminée ». Elle instancie chaque module présent parmi `scenes/{combat,village,world}/<module>_module.tscn`, l'ajoute comme enfant et appelle `attach(valley)`. Un module est un `Node` sans `class_name` s'il utilise des autoloads, et ne parle à la vallée que par son API (CONTRACTS §7) : `get_art_valley()`, `get_defense_grid()`, `get_fx_layer()`, `get_camera()`, `get_tower_view(id)`, `get_hud_action_bar()` (ses boutons), `get_hud_resources_rect()` (panneau des ressources du HUD, en haut à gauche : les éléments centrés en haut s'en écartent), `get_panel_layer()` (ses panneaux, sous les toasts), `show_side_panel(panel)` / `hide_side_panel(panel)` / `side_panel()`, `focus_view(&"defense" | &"village")`, `current_view()`, `set_interaction_locked()`, `is_interaction_locked()`, `set_layout_towers_visible()`, `present_grid()` / `restore_grid()`, `set_resources_frozen()`, `is_planning_open()`, `open_planning()`, `select_building(id)`, `selected_building()`, `clear_selection()`, `modules()`, `game_menu()` ; signaux `building_selected(id)`, `tower_selected(id)`, `view_changed(view)`, `side_panel_changed(panel)`, `loaded()`.

- **Panneaux latéraux** : un seul à la fois entre les modules, arbitré par l'emplacement latéral de la vallée (`show_side_panel` masque le panneau affiché avant, quel que soit son module ; cadre commun `SidePanel`, `scenes/ui/side_panel`). Un panneau est à droite par défaut ; `dock(true)` l'accole à gauche, sous les ressources du HUD ; avec `fit_content`, sa hauteur suit son contenu (jusqu'à la hauteur libre). Sa largeur est celle de sa zone (`SidePanel.area_for`) quel que soit son contenu : un contenu plus large défilerait de côté au lieu d'élargir le panneau ; la fiche de tour (`TowerCard`) passe à la ligne pour tenir dans toute largeur à partir de `MIN_CONTENT_WIDTH`, une valeur trop longue allant sous son nom. Les toasts de l'Overlay évitent les zones déclarées par `Overlay.avoid(control)` : ils passent à gauche d'une zone collée au bord droit (panneau latéral) et sous les autres (bandeau et alerte du titan mondial, bandeau hors ligne). Tant que le parchemin est ouvert, aucun toast ne s'affiche (`Overlay.hold_while_visible`) : rien ne couvre le plateau, les compteurs, la fiche ni la carte d'alerte ; ceux déjà à l'écran le quittent sans jamais revenir (un toast n'est jamais montré deux fois), les nouveaux attendent ; à la fermeture, ceux qui n'ont pas dépassé leur durée d'affichage s'affichent, les autres sont abandonnés (la ligne d'état et la carte d'alerte ont dit la même chose).

content.content:
﻿## Plan : choix de la langue et traduction complète du client (9 langues)

### Décisions techniques

1. **Clés = texte source français** (style gettext), pas de clés UPPER_SNAKE comme LHT1.
   - Les `.tscn` ne changent pas : `text = "Paramètres"` devient le msgid et `auto_translate` le traduit à l'affichage.
   - Les quelque 600 assertions sur du français dans les tests restent vraies, car `Label.text` garde le msgid. Avec des clés UPPER_SNAKE, `button.text` vaudrait `"SETTINGS"` et toutes ces assertions tomberaient.
   - Si une traduction manque, le texte français s'affiche. Les noms du catalogue et les messages du serveur restent en français.
   - De LHT1 (`C:\travaille\godot\towermoulineux\client\ressources\trad\trad.csv`), on ne reprend que la terminologie (glossaire). Attention : ses cellules commencent par des espaces parasites, à nettoyer.
2. **Format : CSV Godot, un fichier par domaine** sous `godot/i18n/<chunk>.csv`. En-tête `keys,en,es,de,ja,ko,zh,pt,ru` : pas de colonne `fr`, puisque le msgid est le texte français.
   - `project.godot` contient `[internationalization] locale/fallback="fr"`. C'est indispensable : le repli par défaut est `en`, qui afficherait de l'anglais en `fr`.
   - Il contient aussi `locale/translations`, qui liste les 8 × N fichiers `.translation` générés. Ils sont tous déclarés dès l'étape 0, donc aucun conflit ensuite sur `project.godot`.
   - `godot/i18n/*.translation` va dans `godot/.gitignore` : ce sont des produits d'import.
3. **Paramètres dans les textes** : uniquement des noms, `{titan}`, `{time}`, avec `String.format()`. On n'utilise plus `%s` dans un msgid, car l'ordre des mots change d'une langue à l'autre (ja, ko).
4. **Pluriels** : une ligne par msgid de la forme `"{n} tour|{n} tours"`. Chaque traduction donne les formes CLDR de sa langue, séparées par `|` :
   - en, es, de, pt : 2 formes ;
   - ru : one/few/many/other, soit 4 ;
   - ja, ko, zh : 1 forme.

   `PluralRules.index(lang, n)` choisit la forme (fr : `|n| < 2` donne le singulier, comme `StatFormat._with_noun`). Cela remplace les quelque 20 motifs `"s" if n > 1`, dont `core/encounter/reward_text.gd:16`, `core/notify/event_messages.gd:75-81`, `scenes/planning/planning_screen.gd:265` et `scenes/village/ui/workshop_panel.gd:242,479`.
5. **Nombres selon la langue** : une table `NumberStyle` par langue (séparateur décimal, séparateur de milliers, espace avant `%`).
   - Le fr garde la typographie de D-198 : `NBSP`, virgule, « 75 % ».
   - en, ja, ko, zh : « 6,000 », « 75% » ; de : « 6.000 », « 75 % » ; ru : NBSP ; es et pt : point pour les milliers.
   - Les unités deviennent des msgids : `"{value} s"`, `"{value} PV"`, `"{value} tir/s"`.
   - `StatFormat`, `TimeUtil.format_duration` et `TitanProfile.decimal_text` (un doublon à router vers `StatFormat`) lisent tous cette table.
6. **Changement de langue à chaud** : `SettingsApplier.apply` appelle `TranslationServer.set_locale()` seulement si la langue change. Le moteur envoie alors `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED` à tout l'arbre.
   - Les textes des `.tscn` suivent seuls.
   - Règle pour chaque script de scène qui écrit un texte en code : `_notification(what)` avec `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED` et `is_node_ready()` relance son `_refresh()` ou `_render()` existant.
   - Les toasts déjà affichés restent dans l'ancienne langue (accepté).
7. **Langue par défaut** : `ProfileSettings.language`, avec comme défaut `LhtLocale.system_language()`.
   - `OS.get_locale_language()` est ramené à l'une des 9 langues (`pt_BR` → `pt`, `zh_TW` → `zh`), sinon `en`.
   - La langue est appliquée dès `Session.configure`, donc avant la scène de démarrage.
8. **Polices** : Noto Sans JP, KR et SC (OFL, google/fonts) sont ajoutées en `fallbacks` sur chaque `FontFile` et `FontVariation` dans `weighted()`.
   - `set_language_support_override` (ja, ko, zh) fait choisir les bons glyphes Han selon la langue.

| planning | `planning.csv` | `core/planning`, `scenes/planning`, `core/domain`, `core/presentation` (sauf `stat_format.gd`) | ~105 |

Règle commune : le français des msgids doit rester identique à l'actuel, pour que les tests restent verts sans modification.

### Étape 2 : intégration (orchestrateur)

- `tests/project/test_i18n_live_switch.gd` : instancier le menu, le HUD de la vallée, le village et la planification, puis passer `fr` → `de` → `en`. Aucun texte visible ne doit rester une traduction `de` différente de sa traduction `en`.
- `tests/project/test_no_hardcoded_french.gd` : recherche dans les `.gd` des littéraux accentués hors `Tx`, `LhtLog` et commentaires, avec une liste d'exceptions dans le fichier. Il vérifie aussi que tout `text` ou `tooltip_text` des `.tscn` existe dans un CSV.
- Captures en fenêtre en `ja`, `ru` et `de` (débordement des panneaux en 1280 × 720).

### Contrats et décisions (orchestrateur)

`docs/v1/CONTRACTS.md` :
- l.5 (conventions) : « textes joueur du client en 9 langues ; textes serveur (catalogue, erreurs, noms de titans) en français ».
- §7 (l.560) : champ `language` de `settings.json`, `godot/i18n/`, msgid français, `{param}`, pluriels `|`, repli `fr`.

`docs/v1/DECISIONS.md` :
- **D-369** : 9 langues, client seulement ; remplace D-004 pour les textes du client (la doc reste en français, le code en anglais).
- **D-370** : msgid français dans des CSV par domaine, repli `fr` ; les clés UPPER_SNAKE de LHT1 ne sont pas reprises.
- **D-371** : paramètres nommés et pluriels CLDR `|`.
- **D-372** : nombres selon la langue ; révise D-198, que le fr conserve.
- **D-373** : langue par défaut = celle du système, sinon `en` ; changement immédiat ; endonymes dans Paramètres.
- **D-374** : polices Noto CJK en repli ; Cinzel retombe sur Alegreya pour le cyrillique.
- **D-375** : tests figés en `fr`.

`CLAUDE.md`, section « Langues » : à mettre à jour.

Aucune modification dans `serveur/` ni `lhtcpp/`.

### Vérification

```bash
G=/c/dev/dev26/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe
$G --headless --path godot --script res://tools/project/build_theme.gd
$G --headless --path godot --import
$G --headless --path godot --script res://tests/run_tests.gd
$G --headless --path godot --script res://tests/run_tests.gd -- --filter=i18n
$G --path godot -- --lht-profile=alice   # changer de langue dans Paramètres, captures
(cd serveur && go test ./...); ctest --test-dir lhtcpp/build-release   # non-régression seulement
```

### Risques

- **Polices** :
  - Taille des polices CJK dans le dépôt : à mesurer à l'étape 0 (repli décrit au point 8).
  - On ne sait pas si `FontVariation` propage bien les replis et l'axe `wght` aux polices CJK : à vérifier sur capture.
  - Même incertitude sur le choix des glyphes Han selon la langue.
- **Imports CSV** : un CSV vide peut ne pas s'importer. Les `.translation` ignorés par git demandent `--import` sur un checkout neuf, ce qui est déjà la règle.
- **Doubles traductions** : un texte déjà traduit en code puis retraduit par `auto_translate` peut, rarement, tomber sur un autre msgid.
- **Renommage** : changer une phrase française rend son msgid orphelin. `test_tx_sources` le détecte.
- **Textes mixtes** : les noms français du serveur insérés dans une phrase anglaise ou japonaise donnent un texte mixte (accepté par l'utilisateur).
- **Mise en page** : textes plus longs en de et ru, débordement des panneaux en 1280 × 720.
- **Fusion** : un msgid identique dans deux chunks avec des traductions différentes fait échouer le test de cohérence ; c'est l'orchestrateur qui tranche.
## 1. Plan de vagues corrigé

**Avant la vague 1 (orchestrateur)**
- Fusionner `v1-instant-buildings` dans `v1`, ou prendre c9ca01c comme base de toutes les branches.
- Créer la branche d'intégration `v1-integration`.
- Prendre une seule série de captures de référence au commit c9ca01c (D-365) : listes `combat`, `village`, `world`, `art_review`, `valley_review`, `menu`, ainsi que `edge_shots`, `top_shots` et `results_shots`. Les plans wait, hp, cam et lang en ont tous besoin.

**Vague 1 : branches en parallèle (worktrees), toutes depuis c9ca01c.** Ordre de fusion : a, b, c, d, e.

**Vague 2 : depuis `v1-integration`, après la vague 1.** Ordre de fusion : f, g, h.

- **f. `v1-w2-towers-client`** (towers C). Fichiers :
  - `core/domain/layout_model.gd`, `core/presentation/valley_text.gd:26-28`, `scenes/planning/planning_screen.gd:238` ;

  Elle passe en vague 2 parce qu'elle partage `event_messages.gd`, `valley_text.gd`, `fake_lht_server.gd`, `test_notifications.gd` et `test_presentation_hold.gd` avec b, et `combat_summary.gd` avec c.

- **g. `v1-w2-towers-balance`** (towers B). Fichiers :

- **h. `v1-w2-combat-camera`** (cam, serveur et client sur une seule branche : un seul agent fait le renommage). Fichiers :

**Vague 3 : extraction des traductions, en dernier.** Sept branches en parallèle `v1-w3-i18n-{shell,net_notify,world,village_core,village_ui,combat,planning}`, depuis `v1-integration` après h.

**Vague 4 : `v1-w4-i18n-integration`** (lang, étape 2), puis les captures `ja`, `ru` et `de`, puis la validation finale.

### lang

1. **Ordre.** L'étape 0 passe en vague 1 : ses chemins sont disjoints de ceux des autres sujets, à vérifier. L'extraction (étape 1) attend la fusion de wait, towers, hp et cam : sinon chaque sujet devrait écrire dans des CSV appartenant à d'autres chunks.
2. **Références inexactes.**

   | Élément | Plan | Code réel |
   |---|---|---|
   | `scale_label` | l.71 | l.68-69 |
   | `"%d %%"` | l.111-112 | l.108-109 |
   | `StatFormat.number` | l.20 | l.21 |
   | `StatFormat.integer` | l.39 | l.41 |

   `StatFormat.percent(bp)` prend des points de base : écrire `percent(roundi(v) * 100)`. Ne pas l'utiliser pour `scale_label`, qui colle déjà NBSP et `%`.
3. **Chunks sans propriétaire.**
   - `core/camera`, `scenes/scene_router.gd` et le `art/**` d'exécution : les attribuer à shell, ou les mettre en exception dans `test_no_hardcoded_french`.
   - Nouveaux chemins des vagues 1 et 2 :
     - `scenes/ui/hp_bar/**` et `combat_hud.tscn` → combat (plutôt que shell) ;
     - `core/presentation/hp_bar_model.gd` → planning.
   - Les msgids `text` et `tooltip_text` des `.tscn` appartiennent au chunk de leur dossier.
4. **Double traduction et noms serveur.** Avec `auto_translate`, un nom du catalogue identique à un msgid (« Atelier », « Temple », « Marchand ») serait traduit à l'affichage. Règle : un `Label` dont le texte est écrit en code (via `Tx` ou avec une donnée serveur) passe en `auto_translate_mode = DISABLED`, et le hook `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED` le rafraîchit.
5. Committer les `godot/i18n/*.csv.import`, qui ne sont pas ignorés. Seuls les `.translation` le sont.
6. `TitanProfile` est dans `core/encounter`, donc dans le chunk combat. L'étape 0 ne touche que `decimal_text`, et le chunk combat part de l'intégration : pas de conflit.
7. Lister dans le brief de la vague 3 les nouveaux msgids des autres sujets :
   - toasts wait ;
   - « Amélioration… » et « Construction… » ;
   - « Tours posées : N » et « W × H cases » (towers) ;
   - pourcentage et repères (hp) ;
   - textes cam (correction cam-5).

## 4. Tests et vérifications à ajouter

- **Après chaque fusion, sur `v1-integration`** :
  ```bash
  (cd serveur && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test ./...)
  $G --import
  $G --script res://tests/run_tests.gd        # 0 failed
  $G -d --script res://tests/check_scripts.gd # 0 WARNING
  $G --script res://art/tests/art_checks.gd
  ```
- **Vague 1**
  - Test de la migration 0064 avec une construction en cours (bogue du point wait-1).
  - `test_combat_hud` : `set_compact(true)` montre exactement une `SegmentedHpBar` et cache `%Feed`.
  - `test_translations_complete` sur des CSV d'amorce.
- **Vague 2**
  - `LHT_BALANCE_REPORT=1` (B), `td_sim_bench` et `real_server_perf` avec 75 tours.
  - E2E `layout_during_combat.gd` et `double_spend.gd`.
  - Go : transfert pendant le verrou, puis rencontre créée en parallèle (sérialisation par `LockState`).
- **Vague 4**
  - `test_i18n_live_switch` doit inclure le `CombatHud` en mode compact et le bandeau mondial segmenté.
  - Captures `ja`, `ru` et `de` du bandeau compact et du pourcentage en 1280 × 720.

## 5. Risques

1. **`combat_module.gd`** : touché par hp (l.171 et l.363) puis cam (focus, vue, bilan), et aussi par lang (combat) en vague 3. Trois passages successifs, jamais en parallèle.
2. **`fake_lht_server.gd`** : touché par b, f et h. Les hunks sont distincts, mais il faut un rebase après chaque fusion.
3. **Équilibrage (B)** : c'est le plus gros risque de durée. Les PV peuvent bouger ; `serveur/data/*.json` est réservé à g pendant la vague 2.
4. **Captures de référence** : elles changent à presque chaque vague. Prendre la référence avant la vague 1, puis une nouvelle à la fin de chaque vague.
5. **Polices CJK** (étape 0 de lang) : le poids du dépôt est à mesurer avant la fusion de d. Le repli « `.res` seuls » doit être tranché par l'orchestrateur.
6. **`v1-instant-buildings`** n'est pas encore dans `v1` : toute branche partie de `v1` reviendrait avant D-368.

class_name Tx
extends RefCounted
## Translation of the client's texts, usable from static code (Object.tr()
## is not). A msgid is the French text itself (res://i18n/<chunk>.csv); a
## missing translation shows the French. Parameters are named, "{titan}", so
## each language orders its words; never "%s" in a msgid.
## Plurals: one msgid "{n} tour|{n} tours" whose translations give the CLDR
## forms of their language separated by "|" (PluralRules).

const PLURAL_SEPARATOR: String = "|"


static func t(msgid: String) -> String:
	return String(TranslationServer.translate(msgid))


## t() with its {placeholders} replaced by `args`.
static func f(msgid: String, args: Dictionary) -> String:
	return t(msgid).format(args)


## The form of `msgid` for `count` (as displayed: round it first), with its
## {placeholders} replaced by `args`; {n} is the count in the language's
## number style unless `args` gives it.
static func n(msgid: String, count: float, args: Dictionary = {}) -> String:
	var translated: String = t(msgid)
	var language: String = LhtLocale.FRENCH if translated == msgid else LhtLocale.current()
	var forms: PackedStringArray = translated.split(PLURAL_SEPARATOR)
	var form: String = forms[clampi(PluralRules.index(language, count), 0, forms.size() - 1)]
	var values: Dictionary = args.duplicate()
	if not values.has("n"):
		values["n"] = NumberStyle.current().number(count)
	return form.format(values)

class_name I18nCsv
extends RefCounted
## One translation table res://i18n/<chunk>.csv, read as text (tests): a
## header "keys,<languages>" and one row per msgid (the French text).

const DIRECTORY: String = "res://i18n"
## Every table; each is declared in project.godot for every language.
const CHUNKS: Array[String] = ["shell", "net_notify", "world", "village_core", "village_ui", "combat", "planning", "common"]
## Translation columns, in the order of the header (French is the msgid).
const LANGUAGES: Array[String] = ["en", "es", "de", "ja", "ko", "zh", "pt", "ru"]
const KEYS_COLUMN: String = "keys"

var chunk: String = ""
var path: String = ""
var header: PackedStringArray = PackedStringArray()
## Every row after the header (blank lines dropped).
var rows: Array[PackedStringArray] = []


static func read(chunk_name: String) -> I18nCsv:
	var table: I18nCsv = I18nCsv.new()
	table.chunk = chunk_name
	table.path = DIRECTORY.path_join(chunk_name + ".csv")
	var file: FileAccess = FileAccess.open(table.path, FileAccess.READ)
	if file == null:
		return table
	table.header = file.get_csv_line()
	while not file.eof_reached():
		var line: PackedStringArray = file.get_csv_line()
		if line.size() == 1 and line[0].is_empty():
			continue
		table.rows.append(line)
	return table


static func read_all() -> Array[I18nCsv]:
	var tables: Array[I18nCsv] = []
	for chunk_name: String in CHUNKS:
		tables.append(read(chunk_name))
	return tables


## The .csv files present in DIRECTORY, without extension, sorted.
static func present_chunks() -> Array[String]:
	var names: Array[String] = []
	for file: String in DirAccess.get_files_at(DIRECTORY):
		if file.get_extension() == "csv":
			names.append(file.get_basename())
	names.sort()
	return names


## msgid -> the translations of its row (language -> text), every table.
static func all_translations() -> Dictionary[String, Dictionary]:
	var by_msgid: Dictionary[String, Dictionary] = {}
	for table: I18nCsv in read_all():
		for row: PackedStringArray in table.rows:
			by_msgid[row[0]] = table.translations_of(row)
	return by_msgid

const REVIEW_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', properties: { issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {

  (impl, b) => {
    if (!impl) return null

      'PLAN CONFORMANCE & TESTS: anything from the task/plan/critique missing or done differently, weak tests, CLAUDE.md convention violations, leftover dead code',
    ]
    return parallel(lenses.map((lens, i) => () => agent(`Adversarial reviewer (${lens}). Review branch ${impl.branch} in worktree ${impl.worktree_path}: \`git -C "${impl.worktree_path}" diff v1...HEAD\`, read the changed code in context. Task given: ${b.task}\nImplementer report: ${impl.summary}\nOpen issues claimed: ${impl.open_issues.join(' | ')}\n${ENV}\nReport ONLY real defects substantiated with concrete evidence.       .then(rs => ({ impl, issues: rs.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.issues).filter(x => x.severity !== 'low'), low: rs.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.issues).filter(x => x.severity === 'low') }))
  },
  (rev, b) => {
    if (!rev) return null

    return agent(`You continue branch ${rev.impl.branch} in its existing worktree ${rev.impl.worktree_path} (cd there; no new worktree or branch).
