tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
La vague 2 est fusionnée dans `v1` et tous les tests passent : Go 33 paquets sur 33, Godot 800 tests sans échec, lint et contrôles d'art OK. La documentation de la vague 2 est commitée (`ac77e62`).

**Ce que la vague 2 apporte :**
- **Tours sans limite** : l'interface affiche « N » tours au lieu de « N / max » et le bilan « W × H cases ». J'ai mesuré 75 tours sur la plus grande grille, contre le vrai serveur : environ 440 images par seconde, aucun ralentissement.
- **Réétalonnage** : les PV des titans de quête et de chasse sont relevés environ ×2,5 à ×3,5, ceux des titans mondiaux ×3, et l'or rapporté par les titans mondiaux ×3 aussi. L'or de la quête est réduit d'un quart, pour que la chasse redevienne utile. Les critères d'équilibrage passent de nouveau, dont les 3 à 6 visites par titan mondial.
- **Liberté pendant un combat** : seule la carte est verrouillée. En vue Village, un bandeau compact affiche le titan, sa barre de PV et un bouton « Voir le combat ». La caméra ne se déplace que pour un combat lancé par le joueur. L'or affiché déduit tout de suite ses propres achats, sans laisser deviner l'issue. Le serveur refuse avec une erreur un transfert vers une tour posée pendant le combat.
- **Tests de bout en bout contre un vrai serveur** : village, parcours complet en 27 étapes, double dépense et disposition pendant un combat, tous verts.

**Deux points à arbitrer :**
- **Combats plus longs** : ils durent environ 2,4 fois plus qu'avant, soit environ 3 min en moyenne et 4 min au plus au palier 10. Plus de tours donnent des labyrinthes plus longs. Je l'ai accepté et consigné en D-372, avec un nouveau critère qui plafonne un combat à 5 min ; la liberté pendant le combat compense en partie. Raccourcir les combats demanderait des titans plus rapides et un nouvel étalonnage complet.
- **Rôle de l'Atelier** : sans limite de tours, la fusion ne sert plus que pour les tours que la grille ne peut pas accueillir. Dans la simulation, elle est 3 à 5 fois moins utilisée. Je ne change rien dans ce chantier.

**En cours :**
- Un agent corrige les petits défauts relevés par les revues : le bilan doit rester devant un panneau du village ouvert après lui, l'or affiché ne doit plus remonter brièvement à « Continuer », et un test Go échoue au hasard. Il rend aussi la base de données configurable dans les scripts de test de bout en bout.
- Un autre agent prépare un glossaire commun pour les 9 langues, reprenant la terminologie de LHT1, ainsi que les traductions partagées entre domaines.

Dès que ces deux agents ont fini, je les fusionne et je lance la vague 3 : les sept branches parallèles qui traduisent toute l'interface.

  - Quests, titans and hunts: Quête principale, Titan mondial, le titan mondial, Chasses, Poser l'appât, Codex des titans, and the related messages.
  - Combat and towers: Dégâts, Portée, Cadence, Ralentissement, Ralenti, Brûlure, Nouvelle tour, `Phase {phase} · {speed} · résistances : {resistances}`, `{hp} / {max_hp} PV`, `{name} · {hp} PV`.
  - Counts: `{amount} or`, `{n} point de QG|{n} points de QG`, `{n} tour|{n} tours`, `{label} : {value}`.
  - Errors: several village and network errors, including Serveur injoignable (same translations as the seed row in `net_notify.csv`).
- **One existing row changed:** in the zh column of `{value} PV`, "{value} 生命值" became "{value}生命值", to follow the zh no-space rule.
- **Glossary:** 188 terms in 9 languages plus a note column. It reuses LHT1's terms where they were sound (titan, tower, HQ, chest, rarities, pt-BR words).

**Style decisions:**
- **Registers:**
  - en: US English, "you".
  - es: neutral Spanish, tú, no vosotros or voseo, with ¡ ¿.
  - de: du (as in LHT1's latest strings), and "Stufe" for level, never "Level".
  - ja: です/ます in sentences, short nouns on buttons, full-width punctuation.
  - ko: 합니다체 for statements, -세요 for instructions, noun buttons, and never a particle attached to a placeholder.
  - zh: Simplified, full-width punctuation, no space between Chinese characters and digits.
  - pt: Brazilian (as in LHT1), você.
  - ru: вы, infinitive buttons, ё always written, « ».
- **Typography:**
  - The French space before `: ! ? ;` is dropped in every other language.
  - An NBSP between a number and its unit is kept wherever the msgid has one.
  - Latin units are separated by a space; CJK units and counters are attached.
  - Quotes per language: en/zh/pt/ko “ ”, de „ “, ja 「」, es/ru « ».
  - Ellipsis is the single `…`, except zh `……`.
  - Separators ` · ` ` — ` ` / ` stay identical in every language.
  - Sentence case everywhere, mirroring the French.
- **Plurals:** 2 forms for en/es/de/pt, 4 for ru, and a single form with a counter for ja/ko/zh (タワー{n}基, 타워 {n}개, {n}座塔).
- **Names inserted into sentences:** placeholders like `{titan}` go where no case inflection is needed (matters for de and ru).
- **§17:** the guide lists the replay words banned in each language. ru Retry is "Попробовать снова", not "Повторить".

**Things the orchestrator should know:**
- **Leading or trailing spaces are rejected.** `test_translations_complete` refuses a space at either end of a msgid or translation. Fragments like `" · stats effectives"`, `" (obtenu)"` and `" (%d affichée%s)"` must become whole msgids with placeholders, or keep the separator in code.
- **NBSP mismatches.** `WorldText.hp_total` prints "300 PV" with a regular space, and `test_world_domain` expects that. The common `{value} PV` row uses an NBSP, so the world chunk should use its own msgid `{hp} PV` instead.
- **Server catalog names that are also client literals.** These will be translated by `auto_translate` unless the label has `auto_translate_mode` disabled: Dégâts, Portée, Cadence, Neutre, Hutte du chasseur, and "Les guildes s'installeront ici plus tard.".
- **API to agree between village_core and village_ui.** `VillageText.countdown` should take a `{time}` template (both templates are in common) instead of gluing a prefix and a duration with `"%s %s"`.
- **Comparisons must stay on msgids.** `spawned == WORLD_TITAN_FALLBACK` and `label.text != done_text` compare constants that will now be translated.
- **Plural hacks:** the 20 `"s" if n > 1` sites are listed per chunk in `i18n_shared.md`.
- **Dates:** the date format should become a reorderable `{day}/{month}/{year}` msgid.

content.text:
La vague 2 et les corrections de sa revue sont fusionnées dans `v1`, et tous les tests passent. La vague 3, qui traduit toute l'interface, tourne en arrière-plan.

**Vérifié sur `v1` fusionnée** (avant les deux fusions suivantes) :
- **Go** : 33 paquets sur 33, y compris l'équilibrage des titans mondiaux qui échouait après la vague 1.
- **Godot** : 800 tests sans échec, lint sans avertissement, contrôles d'art OK.

**Fusionné ensuite** (vérifié par les agents dans leurs branches, pas encore relancé sur `v1`) :
- **Corrections de la revue** (803 tests Godot) :
  - le bilan reste devant un panneau du village ouvert après lui ;
  - l'or affiché ne remonte plus un instant à « Continuer » ;
  - un test Go qui échouait au hasard est stabilisé ;
  - le port de la base de données et le chemin du moteur sont désormais réglables dans les scripts de test de bout en bout.
- **Glossaire commun** : 188 termes en 9 langues et 66 traductions partagées entre les domaines, avec la terminologie de LHT1. Choix de style : allemand en « du » et portugais du Brésil, comme LHT1 ; espagnol en « tú », russe en « вы ».

**Vague 3 en cours** : sept agents traduisent chacun un domaine de l'interface en 8 langues, en gardant le texte français à l'identique. Chaque domaine est ensuite relu par un agent qui cherche les textes oubliés, les erreurs de traduction et tout équivalent de « rejeu », puis corrigé.

**À trancher par toi** (consigné dans D-372) :
- **Combats plus longs** : un combat dure environ 2,4 fois plus qu'avant, soit 3 minutes en moyenne au palier 10. C'est l'effet des labyrinthes plus longs, maintenant que les tours sont illimitées. Un nouveau critère plafonne un combat à 5 minutes, et pendant ce temps le joueur peut circuler librement. Les raccourcir demanderait des titans plus rapides et un nouvel étalonnage complet.
- **Atelier** : la fusion ne sert presque plus, puisque la grille accueille toutes les tours. Je n'ai rien changé à son rôle.

La documentation de la vague 2 est à jour (décisions D-372, D-373 et D-378 à D-381, contrats, état et plan). Je fusionnerai les sept branches de traduction dès qu'elles seront terminées, puis je passerai à la vague 4 : test de changement de langue à chaud, test qu'aucun texte français ne reste en dur, captures en japonais, russe et allemand.

## v1-w3-i18n-combat
- « Hutte du chasseur » (the hunts panel subtitle) is a msgid in combat.csv, translated as in the glossary. If village_ui or village_core also adds it, the two rows must have identical translations (test_a_msgid_shared_by_two_tables). The orchestrator may want to move it to common.csv.
- SidePanel (scenes/ui/side_panel, outside my paths) still auto-translates its own title, subtitle and error labels and the « Fermer » button. My panels pass already-translated titles, so the risk is a second translation only if a translated title equals another msgid. Its owner should decide on DISABLED there.
- TitanProfile.resistances_text still joins its items with « , » in every language. ja and zh would prefer 、/，, but test_translations_complete forbids leading or trailing spaces, so a separator cannot be a msgid.
- HuntsPanel.set_blocked and MsqPanel.set_blocked receive reasons that are already translated. combat_module re-sends the world-visit reason on a language change, but village_module (another chunk) must do the same for the hut panel's FIGHT_SHOWN reason.
- Error lines and announcements already shown keep their language after a switch (same as toasts).
- Gold amounts in reward texts stay ungrouped (« 1200 or »), as before; switching them to NumberStyle would change French output (« 1 200 or »).

## v1-w3-i18n-net_notify
- Possible double translation by the toast overlay (shell chunk): toasts now arrive already translated. If the overlay's toast Label still has auto_translate on, a translated toast that happens to equal a msgid would be translated again. The overlay toast labels should use AUTO_TRANSLATE_MODE_DISABLED.
- Messages built by other chunks: some code passes ErrorMessages output into its own French sentences, for example planning_session "Aperçu du chemin indisponible : %s" and planning_screen "Placement refusé : %s". Those outer sentences belong to the planning chunk; the inner text is now translated.
- Possible duplicate msgids from parallel chunks: some of my msgids, such as "Erreur", "Or insuffisant." or "Points de QG insuffisants.", might also be added by village_core or village_ui, which have similar texts. test_a_msgid_shared_by_two_tables_has_the_same_translations would then require identical translations in every table. If two tables end up with one of these, the orchestrator should move it to common.csv.
- Russian gender in the kill toasts: ru uses masculine forms such as "{titan} повержен…". This is fine for "мировой титан" and the current titan names, but a feminine server titan name would read slightly off.

## v1-w3-i18n-planning
- Shell chunk: tower_card.gd shows the TowerSheet texts, which are already translated here, and the hint passed as Tx.t(HINT). Its labels must be set to AUTO_TRANSLATE_MODE_DISABLED: catalog names such as 'Dégâts'/'Portée'/'Cadence' (modifiers) or 'Neutre' (element) would otherwise be translated. tower_card.gd:124 also appends ' · stats effectives' to placement_text and needs its own msgid '{placement} · stats effectives'.
- World chunk: hud.gd displays ValleyText.tier(), grid() and towers(), which are now translated at call time; the HUD must re-render on NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED and use non-auto-translated labels for these values. valley_selection.gd shows ValleyText.building_tag with the server building name, so that label needs DISABLED.
- village_core: village_text.gd calls ValleyText.building_state(), which now returns translated text; the labels showing it should be DISABLED and re-rendered on a language change.
- Possible cross-chunk duplicates: if another chunk also adds 'Entrée', 'Sortie', 'Construit', 'Posée', 'Toutes' or 'Disposition enregistrée.', test_a_msgid_shared_by_two_tables_has_the_same_translations requires identical translations. These may be worth moving to common.csv at merge time; planning.csv is the only chunk table that defines them on this branch.
- The en translation of the common msgid '{value} tir/s' is '{value} shots/s', which reads '1 shots/s'. That row belongs to common.csv; the orchestrator may want a plural there.

## v1-w3-i18n-shell
- Possible conflict when merging: if another chunk (for example world/hud) also adds the msgids « En ligne » or « Hors ligne », test_a_msgid_shared_by_two_tables_has_the_same_translations requires identical translations. They may also belong in common.csv; the orchestrator should decide.
- For the orchestrator: a message for i18n_shared.md. Shell decided to put the bullet in code, not in the msgid, because of the glyph test. Other chunks that put symbols in msgids (●, ◔, ✓, ✕) will hit the same font check.
- For the planning chunk: planning_screen calls TowerCard.show_hint(HINT). It should pass Tx.t(HINT) and call it again on NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED, because the card no longer auto-translates the hint.

## v1-w3-i18n-village_core
- Needed in village_ui (building_panel.gd:115-116, outside my paths): refresh_clock compares `label.text != done_text`, but countdown() now returns Tx.t(done_text). In any language other than French, `was_running` would stay true, so the panel would ask the server for the new state on every refresh after zero. The comparison must use Tx.t(done_text) or VillageText.countdown(0.0, prefix, done_text). Countdown labels must also be set to AUTO_TRANSLATE_MODE_DISABLED.
- village_ui callers still pass the bare prefix "Prêt dans" (building_panel TIMER_PREFIX and add_countdown defaults). This works through PREFIX_TEMPLATES, but they could switch to VillageText.READY_IN.
- Still needed in village_ui: workshop_panel returns VillageText.IN_LAYOUT raw (lines 245 and 321), and it needs Tx.t(VillageText.IN_LAYOUT) at display. The msgid is in village_core.csv.
- Planning chunk dependency: VillageText.level_text/subtitle call ValleyText.building_state, and TransferSelection._property_text uses TowerSheet row.label/value and neighbor_text. Their translation depends on that chunk. Here they are only joined with "%s %s" or inserted as {bonus}.
- The ', ' separator between the odds in ChestOffer.contents_text stays in code. ja and zh would normally use '、'. I judged this minor.

## v1-w3-i18n-village_ui
- Possible clashes with msgids of other chunks (test_a_msgid_shared_by_two_tables requires identical translations): 'Retirer', 'Choisir', 'Coût', 'En cours…', 'Fusion', 'Transfert', 'Catalyseur', 'QG', 'Points de QG', 'Amélioration', 'Construction', 'Or insuffisant : {amount} requis.'. I used the glossary forms exactly, but planning, village_core or combat might add the same msgid with different text. The orchestrator should check at merge, and may move them to common.csv.
- Texts that come from village_core (VillageText.subtitle, refusal_text, cost_text, unlocks_line, duration_text, date_time_text, codex_state, IN_LAYOUT, FINISHING/ALMOST, FusionSelection/TransferSelection previews) are shown as returned. With the panel auto-translate off, they show in French until village_core translates them with Tx. VillageText.IN_LAYOUT, FINISHING and ALMOST are passed through Tx.t here and need rows in village_core.csv.
- Errors already shown (the SidePanel error line, the merchant and hut load errors, toasts) keep the language they were written in when the language changes, as accepted for toasts. The Temple message is reloaded.
- SidePanel (scenes/ui/side_panel, outside my paths) still writes 'Fermer' and relies on auto-translate; the shell chunk owns it.

## v1-w3-i18n-world
- SidePanel (scenes/ui/side_panel, not in my paths): its _title, _subtitle and _error labels still auto-translate, and its 'Fermer' close button is a raw literal that relies on auto-translation. WorldPanel only disables body(); the SidePanel owner should convert 'Fermer' to Tx.t and disable those labels.
- These world.csv msgids may also be used by other chunks: 'Menu principal', 'Reprendre', 'Quitter le jeu', 'Défense', 'Village', 'Parchemin', 'Coup fatal' (and the seed 'Menu'). If shell, planning or combat add the same msgid, the orchestrator should move it to common.csv. Glossary translations were used to ease that.
- The HUD tier value text comes from ValleyText.tier ('Palier N'), translated by the planning chunk. The hover tag and the tower card come from ValleyText.building_tag and TowerSheet (planning) and from TowerCard (shell).
- An announcement already on screen keeps its main text in the language of its arrival (accepted, like toasts).
- No windowed captures were taken of the translated world UI (ja, ru, de at 1280×720). Left to the 5.4 integration wave.
- docs/v1/DECISIONS.md should record the inflection rule for {titan}/{killer} and the per-language placement choices above.

- Kept the ▼ arrow out of the msgid: test_theme's glyph check failed because Cinzel has no ▼. The msgid is « Faites défiler pour voir la suite du bilan » and the code adds the ▼ prefix (CombatResultsPanel.MORE_ARROW). French output is unchanged.
- My msgids « Coup fatal ! » and « Vous avez porté le coup fatal à {titan} ! » use an ordinary space before « ! », as the existing combat_summary tests expect. world_text uses the same texts with NBSP, so these are separate msgids from the world chunk's.
- The plural count passed to Tx.n is the displayed value, rounded to 0.1 (range, shots/s, speed). French differs from before only in the 1.95–1.99 band, which used to show « 2 case ».
- RewardText.prim_text now uses common.csv's StatFormat.CELLS_TEXT and SECONDS_TEXT (NBSP, real plural) for units and ticks; no test covers those branches. tower_stats_text and effect_text keep their own ordinary-space msgids, which tests pin.
- Server texts stay raw: catalog names, the lowercase rarity in « Tour {rarity} » and the reason code in « Chasse indisponible ({reason}). ». Translations avoid case or gender agreement around {titan}: ru and ko put the name after « : » or reword (« Бой продолжается: {titan}. », « Титан повержен: {titan}. »), and de and ru put the rarity in parentheses.

- Rather than disabling auto-translation at panel or container roots, I set it per label for the results panel, which holds TowerCard, and on SidePanel.body() for the hunts and main-quest panels. This avoids changing how the shell chunk's TowerCard and SidePanel behave.

## v1-w3-i18n-net_notify 96
- "titan_name()" still returns the French msgid "le titan mondial", so the check `spawned == WORLD_TITAN_FALLBACK` is unchanged. Translation happens only for display, in a new private EventMessages._shown_titan(), and _capitalized() runs after translation (en gives "The world titan…", de "Der Welttitan…").
- Counts and dimensions in the toasts and reward summary are passed as str(n), not NumberStyle, so the French output is byte-identical; "1500 or" stays ungrouped in every language. This follows the rule in i18n_shared.md for code that used %d.
- "Votre grille s'agrandit : {width} × {height}, jusqu'à {capacity} tours." is a plain msgid as the hints suggested, not Tx.n, because capacity is always above 1. ru avoids the noun agreement with "максимум башен: {capacity}".
- Where a case-inflected language would have to decline {titan}, the sentence is reworded to keep it in subject position or after a colon. For example, de uses "Der Kampf beginnt. Gegner: {titan}." and ru "Начинается бой. Противник: {titan}.". ko attaches no particle to a placeholder ("{killer} 님이 {titan} 처치에 성공했습니다!").
- The client-side ApiError.message texts in api_client and the services' "X invalide : {detail}" are translated as the hints asked, even though most of them are covered by an _ERRORS entry and rarely reach the screen. They also show up in logs in the player's language.
- I removed the seed row "Serveur injoignable" from net_notify.csv because it duplicates common.csv, and the table now has other rows.
- There is no scene in my paths, so instead of a NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED scene check, the test confirms that messages built after LhtLocale.apply("de") are in German and return to French afterwards. Toasts already shown keep their language, which is the accepted behaviour.

## v1-w3-i18n-planning 59
- Fixed texts of the planning screen (built in code: title, subtitle, legend, footer buttons, tooltip, banner, dialog title/body/buttons, filter 'Toutes' toggles, checkbox) are kept as msgid literals translated by the engine's auto-translation, so .text stays the French msgid (tests and press_dialog_button keep working in any language); only labels whose text is computed in code use Tx with AUTO_TRA
- The planning status line and a refusal already on screen keep the language they were written in when the language changes, as accepted for toasts. The counters, inventory, card and board are written again.
- Counts that were printed with %d (towers in the inventory, coordinates, damage, tier) are passed as str(n) to keep the French output identical: no digit grouping, unlike NumberStyle.
- Placeholder names: {length} for the recomputed path length (the hint suggested {detail}), {reason} for the refusal, {towers} and {size} for the counters, {x}/{y}, {damage}/{range}/{rate}, {percent}/{duration}, {id}, {tier}, {error}.
- 'Annuler les modifications' (revert to the confirmed layout) and 'Abandonner les modifications' (discard on close) get distinct translations in every language, e.g. en 'Revert changes' / 'Discard changes', ru 'Отменить изменения' / 'Отбросить изменения'.
- Key names in the hint: fr 'Suppr' becomes en Delete, es Supr, de Entf, and Delete in ja/ko/zh/pt/ru; 'Échap' becomes Esc in every language.

## v1-w3-i18n-shell 44
- Connection status: the msgids are « En ligne » / « Hors ligne », and the bullet is added in code ("● %s"). The shared hint said to keep the bullet in the msgid, but test_theme::test_every_translated_character_has_a_glyph fails because the Alegreya and Cinzel fonts have no glyph for U+25CF.

- TowerCard.show_hint(text) expects text that is already translated, and the caller re-renders it on a language change. The card's own default hint « Aucune tour sélectionnée. » is re-rendered by the card. On a language change the card shows its current TowerSheet again as it is; the owner rebuilds the sheet to translate the sheet's own texts.
- Not translated, because they only go to the logs or are replaced by the ErrorMessages table: LaunchOptions warnings, profile_store read/remove/quarantine errors, the INVALID_RESPONSE messages in session_manager and catalog_repository. The profile_store write_json errors are translated because they reach the « Enregistrement local impossible » toast.
- A boot failure already on screen keeps its texts when the language changes, the same rule as toasts. The language cannot change on the boot screen anyway.
- The titles « Last Hit Titan 2 » are not added as rows; their labels are DISABLED. « Défendez l'accès à la Montagne Sacrée » and « Quitter » are in shell.csv. art/**, scene_router, input, camera, catalog_data and dict_reader have no player text.

## v1-w3-i18n-village_core 50
- VillageText.countdown(seconds_left, template = READY_IN, done_text = FINISHING) has the same positional signature as before. `template` can be a msgid with {time} ("Prêt dans {time}" / "De nouveau disponible dans {time}", both from common). The old bare prefixes "Prêt dans" and "De nouveau disponible dans" are mapped through PREFIX_TEMPLATES. Any other prefix falls back to "%s %s" with Tx.t(prefix
- ChestOffer.COOLDOWN_PREFIX is now the template VillageText.AVAILABLE_AGAIN_IN ("De nouveau disponible dans {time}"). merchant_panel passes it through add_countdown to countdown, so its French output is unchanged.
- The QG refusal is one whole plural sentence, "Points de QG insuffisants : {required} requis, {n} disponible.|…disponibles.", not a sentence plus a separate `{n} disponible` fragment. In es and pt it is worded "necesitas X, tienes Y" / "você precisa de X e tem Y" to avoid agreement with the number.
- The fusion input count became a plural msgid. In French, n=1 now reads "Choisissez 1 tour …" instead of the ungrammatical "1 tours". No test covers n=1 in French.
- For %d values I pass str(n) explicitly (QG points, levels, tower and catalyst counts) so French output keeps no thousands grouping. Gold amounts go through StatFormat.integer (NumberStyle).
- BuildingStatus.action_text() and busy_text() return translated text (Tx.t), like the VillageText functions.
- VillageText.unlocks_line's empty_text default is now the constant NOTHING_MORE ("rien de plus"), and the value is translated at use.
- For the "one scene re-renders on NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED" requirement, my paths contain no scene. Instead, the test checks that the VillageText and BuildingStatus texts change after LhtLocale.apply('de') and come back after 'fr'.

## v1-w3-i18n-village_ui 95
- BuildingPanel sets auto_translate_mode = DISABLED on the whole panel, because SidePanel's title, subtitle and error labels belong to another chunk and are private, and the panel title is a server name (collision 'Hutte du chasseur'). The SidePanel 'CloseButton' is set back to ALWAYS through footer().get_node_or_null(), so it keeps whatever translation the shell chunk gives it. Anything the shell o
- The countdown text is computed in BuildingPanel.countdown_text() and no longer calls VillageText.countdown(), so it does not depend on the API village_core chooses. add_countdown(prefix) accepts the msgid 'Prêt dans {time}' (the new default) or a bare prefix, which gets ' {time}' appended. Both paths end on the common msgids.
- The arrow line of the workshop's transfer tab is split into 3 msgids joined by ' → ' in code. test_theme requires every translated character to have a glyph in Cinzel, which has no '→'. ' → ' is a layout separator in the style guide, and the French output is unchanged.
- The fusion help text and 'Déjà {n} tours choisies.' use Tx.n even though the French count is always ≥ 2: Russian needs башни/башен agreement. The French singular forms exist only to complete the plural pair.
- The 'un inconnu' killer stand-in is translated to match its own sentence (de dative 'einem Unbekannten', ru nominative after 'добил:'), because it replaces a player name and no inflection is applied to it.
- BuildingStatus.action_text() and busy_text() are passed through Tx.t when shown. This works whether village_core returns msgids or text that is already translated.

## v1-w3-i18n-world 75
- WorldText constants and the SKIP_REASONS values stay French msgids, translated at display (Tx.t). WorldText.MSGIDS lists them for the tests.
- WorldText.titan_name now returns the translated fallback Tx.t(FALLBACK_NAME). EventMessages keeps its own untranslated WORLD_TITAN_FALLBACK for its comparison.
- WorldAnnouncement.title and .detail hold msgids that the view translates and redraws on a language change. .text is rendered when the event arrives and keeps that language, like a toast.
- recent_line: the fragments 'abattu', 'votre coup fatal' and 'coup fatal de {killer}' are msgids, and the '%s — %s, %s' join stays in code (per i18n_shared.md). contribution() keeps the '%s (%s)' join.
- ago(): 'il y a {n} min/h/j' get {n} as str(int), so the French output is unchanged.
- Server titan names are never inflected. In es, pt, de and ru, {titan} sits in subject position or after a colon (e.g. de 'Durch deinen Todesstoß fällt {titan}!', ru 'Вы нанесли добивающий удар: {titan}!'). In ko, placeholders are never followed by a particle.
- 'WARNING — TITAN EN APPROCHE !' is translated in the other languages (WARNING/ALERTA/WARNUNG/警告/경고/ВНИМАНИЕ) rather than keeping the English word.
- The HUD tier tooltip follows the last shown completion state (_tier_completed), so a language change during a frozen fight shows nothing new. The tier label itself is redrawn only when the values are not frozen.
- HUD icons-only mode: a button that has a stashed text and now non-empty text was rewritten by its owner, so its new text and tooltip are kept and stashed again.
- game_menu._button and hud._value/_bar_button (private) changed signatures. game_menu._button is no longer static. No public signature changed.

Écarte des replis statiques dans le thème : Godot prend l'ascendante et la descendante les plus grandes de la chaîne (ligne d'Inter 22 px de 28 à 33 px, `test_results_layout` cassé en français). 1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user wants the five items from the LHT2 (Last Hit Titan 2) meeting implemented end to end. Ultracode is on, so multi-agent workflows are opted in. The approved plan is `C:\Users\akitl\.claude\plans\nifty-rolling-crane.md`.
   - **(1) Languages:** a language-selection menu plus a full client translation into 9 languages (fr, en, es, de, ja, ko, zh, pt, ru).
     - The agent writes the translations, reusing the terminology of LHT1's `C:\travaille\godot\towermoulineux\client\ressources\trad\trad.csv`.
     - Client only: server texts stay French.
     - The default is the OS language, otherwise English. A change applies immediately and is stored in the local profile (Paramètres).
   - **(2) Construction:** remove the construction waiting system on both client and server.
   - **(3) Towers:** no tower limit while a valid path exists. Capacity is optional (`null` = unlimited), and the HP and rewards of the titans are re-tuned.
   - **(4) Titan HP:** readable HP portions:
     - phase dividers ▲;
     - MSQ reward markers ◆, greyed once claimed;
     - a percentage;
     - a hatched `initial_hp` zone for the world titan.
   - **(5) Free movement during a fight**, from engagement to « Continuer »:
     - Only the map is locked; the server lock is unchanged.
     - In the Village view, a compact banner shows the titan with a « Voir le combat » button.
     - The results show whatever the view.
     - The camera moves only for a fight the player launched.
     - Displayed gold = gold before the fight minus the player's own spending (§17).
   - The user asked « c'est terminé ? » mid-way and was told no: wave 4 was still to come.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:**
     - Godot 4.7.2 client (GDScript, static typing).
     - Authoritative Go 1.24 server (pgx, Postgres 17).
     - Deterministic C++20 engine `td_sim_cli`.
   - **i18n:**
     - The msgid is the current French text, stored in `godot/i18n/<chunk>.csv` (header `keys,en,es,de,ja,ko,zh,pt,ru`), with `locale/fallback="fr"`.
     - Helpers `Tx.t/f/n` with named `{params}`; CLDR plural forms separated by `|` (ru 4 forms, ja/ko/zh 1).
     - `NumberStyle` formats numbers per language.
     - Labels whose text is set in code use `auto_translate_mode` DISABLED and refresh on `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED`.
     - Tests are pinned to fr. Symbols without a glyph (●, ▼, →) are kept out of msgids.
     - Chunks: shell, net_notify, world, village_core, village_ui, combat, planning, common.
   - **Workflow pattern per wave:** implement in a worktree → adversarial review → fix → the orchestrator merges into `v1` and updates `docs/v1`.
   - **Balance:** `layout.Slots(grid)` gives 14, 24, 27, 44, 52 and 75 slots for the six grids; criteria C1–C5 (C5 = no fight over 5 min).
   - **Presentation hold:**
     - `GameState.note_own_spending`, `apply_village(data, own)`, `apply_own_inventory`, `mask_held_balance`, and the signal `held_spending_applied`.
     - An own operation drops the held snapshots read before it.
   - **Server:** a transfer onto a placed tower under the layout lock returns 409 `layout_locked`.

Quest HP 150, 760, 1050, 2050, 2200, 2400, 3850, 4950, 5700, 9300; hunts 80 / 1800 / 4800; world HP per player 5400 / 6000 / 7200; `hp_per_gold` 150; quest gold ×0.75 (kill 25 to 190); fights 2.4× longer, accepted; C5; fusion role to revisit.

# Plan — 5 retours de réunion (langues, construction, tours, PV du titan, liberté en combat)

## Context
La réunion a produit 5 demandes sur la V1 jouable :
1. un menu de choix de la langue ;
2. retirer le reliquat de l'attente de construction (les améliorations sont immédiates depuis D-368, mais le système
   et ses traces UI existent toujours) ;
3. aucune limite de tours tant qu'un chemin reste valide ;
4. rendre lisibles les portions de vie du titan ;
5. pendant le passage d'un titan, pouvoir circuler librement (village, menus) — seule la carte reste non modifiable
   (la note « toujours focus la zone de fight » était une erreur de transcription).

Exploration (`wf_841e5b6c-96a`) et conception (`wf_d68636ea-956` : 5 agents Plan + critique d'intégration) faites.
Plans détaillés par sujet (chemins, lignes, tests) — à transmettre tels quels aux agents d'implémentation, avec les
corrections de la critique :
`C:\Users\akitl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--travaille-godot-towermoulineux2\7020066a-783a-415a-a50d-d8623080aee1\scratchpad\`
`plan_lang.md`, `plan_wait.md`, `plan_towers.md`, `plan_hp.md`, `plan_cam.md`, `critique.md`.

## Arbitrages de l'utilisateur (à consigner en D-369…)
| Sujet | Décision |
|---|---|
| Langues | fr, en, es, de, ja, ko, zh, pt, ru (comme LHT1). Client seul : catalogue, erreurs et noms venant du serveur restent en français. Défaut = langue de l'OS sinon anglais ; changement immédiat ; réglage dans le profil local (Paramètres). Traductions produites par l'agent, terminologie reprise de `C:\travaille\godot\towermoulineux\client\ressources\trad\trad.csv`. Remplace D-004 pour le client. |
| Construction | Suppression client **et** serveur (révise D-368). |
| Tours | Capacité **optionnelle** : `capacity: null` = illimité, toute la V1 illimitée ; limites réelles = tours possédées, place, chemin (`no_path` du moteur), garde-fou 256. **Réétalonnage** des PV/récompenses jusqu'au retour des critères D-270/D-224. |

# LHT2 — Instructions agent

LHT-2 (Last Hit Titan 2) : client Godot 4.7, serveur Go autoritaire, simulateur de combat natif déterministe (C++). Le chantier en cours est la **V1 jouable de bout en bout** définie par `docs/V1_scope_prompt.md`.

## Reprise de contexte
Au démarrage d'une session ou après un résumé de contexte, **lire d'abord** `docs/v1/STATUS.md` puis `docs/v1/PLAN.md`, et au besoin `docs/v1/CONTRACTS.md` (interfaces sim ↔ serveur ↔ client) et `docs/v1/DECISIONS.md` (arbitrages et règles V1).

## Sources de vérité (hiérarchie, scope §2)
1. `docs/V1_scope_prompt.md` — décisions validées pour la V1. Méthode : §46–49. Acceptation : §50–56. Définition de terminé : §56.
2. `docs/LHT2_GDD_v0.3.md` — règles de game design non redéfinies par le scope. « À définir » = règle manquante (tranchée dans `DECISIONS.md`) ; « Base de travail » = valeur provisoire. Données des tours : `docs/LHT2_Stat_GDD - Tower.csv` (= Annexe A).
3. `docs/v1/CONTRACTS.md` — contrats techniques V1 (normatifs pendant le chantier).

# LHT2 — Instructions agent
